newsitem.title: MEXICO: Former Chiapas envoy testified in Colosio case.
newsitem.headline: Former Chiapas envoy testified in Colosio case.

text.p: Former Chiapas peace envoy Manuel Camacho Solis has testified in a probe into the 1994 slaying of a top Mexican politician, the attorney general's office said on Sunday.

Camacho, also a former mayor of Mexico City and a former foreign minister, joined ex-president Carlos Salinas de Gortari and top Salinas aide Jose Cordoba Montoya on the list of high-profile figures to have given evidence in recent weeks in the assassination of Luis Donaldo Colosio.

Colosio was the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party's (PRI) candidate for president when he was shot to death on March 23, 1994 in the most serious political killing in Mexico in half a century.
"Manuel Camacho Solis appeared as a witness at the beginning of the second half of November and answered the questions put to him," the attorney general's office said in a brief statement.
Camacho was Salinas's first peace envoy to Zapatista guerrillas, who rose up in arms on New Year's Day 1994 in the southeastern state of Chiapas.

His high-profile dealings with the rebels stole public attention away from Colosio's campaign for president, giving rise to allegations that he was seeking to displace Colosio as the ruling party candidate, possibly with the backing of Salinas.

Luis Raul Gonzalez Perez, the fourth special investigator to probe the killing, has been examining the political circumstances surrounding Colosio's death, including allegations of tension between Colosio and Salinas and reports of efforts to persuade Colosio to step down.

One man is serving a 45-year sentence for shooting Colosio in the head at a campaign rally in the northern city of Tijuana, but prosecutors are convinced the killing was a plot involving other people.

Salinas gave evidence last week at the Mexican embassy in Dublin, where he lives in self-imposed exile. He is expected to testify again this week in connection to another 1994 killing of a top politician, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, for which his elder brother, Raul, faces murder charges.
Salinas, Camacho and Cordoba have all denied any involvement in the respective killings.
